note: Free movement of workers in the European Economic Area and Switzerland: a national of an EU Member State may live in another for longer than three months as a worker or self-employed person (Directive 2004/38 art. 7) and is treated as its nationals are (art. 24); the EEA Joint Committee incorporated the Directive into the EEA Agreement, extending it to Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway; the EU–Swiss Agreement on the free movement of persons gives Swiss nationals and the EU's the same in each other's territory, the residence permit issued as of right on a contract of employment. So none needs a permission to work there (taken as free; registering residence is a formality, not modelled). Liechtenstein's own quota on EEA nationals' residence is its rule apart.

sources.title: Publications Office of the EU, Directive 2004/38/EC on the right of citizens of the Union and their family members to move and reside freely within the territory of the Member States, articles 7 and 24
sources.said: Right of residence for more than three months 1. All Union citizens shall have the right of residence on the territory of another Member State for a period of longer than three months if they: (a) are workers or self-employed persons in the host Member State; ... all Union citizens residing on the basis of this Directive in the territory of the host Member State shall enjoy equal treatment with the nationals of that Member State within the scope of the Treaty.

sources.title: Publications Office of the EU, Decision of the EEA Joint Committee No 158/2007 amending Annex V and Annex VIII to the EEA Agreement
sources.said: is to be incorporated into the Agreement.

sources.title: Publications Office of the EU, Agreement between the European Community and its Member States and the Swiss Confederation on the free movement of persons, Annex I, article 6
sources.said: An employed person who is a national of a Contracting Party (hereinafter referred to as "employed person") and is employed for a period of one year or more by an employer in the host state shall receive a residence permit which is valid for at least five years from its date of issue.
